stem.text: The function h is continuous on the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \) and twice differentiable on \( (-1, 6) \), with \( h'(3) = 0 \) and \( h''(3) < 0 \). Must h attain an absolute maximum value on the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: Yes, because h is continuous on the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem applies.

worked_solution.text: The interval \( [-1, 6] \) is closed and bounded.
The function h is continuous on the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \).
Both hypotheses of the Extreme Value Theorem hold, so h attains an absolute maximum value on \( [-1, 6] \). The theorem gives existence only, not where the value occurs.
